chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Salih ibn Uqbah from Yunus al-Shaybani who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man sells a transaction, and the seller knows it is not worth its price, and the buyer knows it is not worth its price, except that he knows he will return to it and buy it from him. He said: 'O Yunus, indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jabir ibn Abdillah: How are you when injustice becomes prevalent and humiliation is bequeathed to you?' He said to him: 'May I not be left to that time, and when will that be? With my father and mother be it.' He said: 'When usury becomes prevalent.' O Yunus, and this is usury, and even if you do not buy it from him, he will return it to you.' I said: Yes.' He said: 'Do not approach it, do not approach it.'

key_terms.لَا تَقْرَبَنَّهُ: Do not approach it (repeated for emphasis)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes usury in a sale where the item is undervalued and repurchased?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the specific commercial practice of 'bay' al-gharar' (sale of uncertainty) or 'bay' al-murabaha' to the broader eschatological sign of the prevalence of *riba*, citing the Prophet’s dialogue with Jabir ibn Abd Allah. The Imam clarifies that even if the buyer intends to repurchase the item, the initial sale with known undervaluation constitutes usury, urging believers to avoid it entirely. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual and economic corruption caused by *riba* as a precursor to greater societal injustice.
